Bukayo Saka has arrived at a career crossroads. We will soon learn whether he is destined to be a good Arsenal player or if he will elevate himself to the level of Premier League, Champions League and England great.

This weekend Saka turns 25, an age when footballers typically enter their peak. Although his legendary status at Arsenal is secure as a title winner, the reaction to the champions’ transfer window suggests there is a general feeling that he can and should produce more to earn “world class” status.

Mikel Arteta is short of such an attacker. He spent the summer investigating whether players of Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez’s calibre might add much-needed stardust to his front three. Failure to secure a big-name forward has led many to conclude that Arsenal’s title defence will be in the mould of their impressive, but cautious 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

"It's another tough game"Ben White on coming up against Chelsea's front three 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/gfazGGNSA8

It is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”

Arsenal: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.Substitutes: Kepa, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman.

How chaotic will Arsenal allow the game to become today? Both of Chelsea’s league matches this season have been remarkably open, to the point of silliness. Arsenal do not usually allow such things to happen on their watch. They are far too sensible for that. But, having seen Brighton create so many chances at Stamford Bridge last week, Arteta may fancy his team to do some serious damage to Chelsea’s damage if the match opens up.

There’s a slight surprise in Chelsea’s line-up with Levi Colwill dropping to the bench and Josh Acheampong coming in. That could point to Alonso changing to a back four with Acheampong at right-back and Pedro Neto playing further forwards as a right winger. Chelsea only managed 25 per cent of possession against Brighton, so is this an attempt to get more of the ball? As expected, Moises Caicedo is not fit so Reece James and Romeo Lavia will need to play well.

A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. So far this season, Joao Pedro has scored and assisted in both league games. Gyokeres, by contrast, has played zero minutes.

They have just got back under way in the second half on Merseyside and Manchester United have taken the lead against Everton through Bryan Mbeumo. You can follow the action from the Hill Dickinson here.

Will Ezri Konsa come into Arsenal’s starting lineup today? It would be harsh on Cristhian Mosquera, who has been excellent so far this season, but when you pay more than £50m for a ready-made, elite-level centre-back, these are the matches you surely want him for. Mosquera had a slight injury against Aston Villa on Monday night, which may give Arteta the perfect reason to throw his new signing into the side.

Today:Everton 0 Manchester United 0 HTArsenal vs Chelsea 4.30pm

Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

“We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”

Chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

#1601. Monza vs Atalanta BC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 06 Nov 2026 21:34

Atalanta BC will be looking to end a six-match winless run across all competitions when they travel to Monza on Sunday for matchday 11 of the Serie A campaign.

Maurizio Sarri's side sit 13th in the Italian top-flight table after collecting just 11 points from their opening 10 matches, leaving them four points above the relegation zone, where the hosts occupy 18th place.

Atalanta's struggles have continued into November, with a 3-0 home defeat to Parma in their most recent league outing leaving them without a Serie A victory in four matches since beating Venezia 3-1 on October 12.

That run has contributed to La Dea's weakest start to a Serie A season since 2014-15, having managed just three victories from their opening 10 fixtures, during which they have scored 16 goals and conceded 20, highlighting the need for greater balance at both ends of the pitch.

Sarri's men head into this encounter on the back of a 1-1 draw against Kairat Almaty at the New Balance Arena, where Nikola Krstovic scored an 82nd-minute equaliser, leaving the Bergamo outfit 16th in the league-phase table and still without a win in six outings across all competitions.

Atalanta will also be looking to secure their first league victory away from home this weekend after collecting just one point from their opening four Serie A away fixtures, although that came in their most recent trip, a 2-2 draw against Fiorentina.

Sarri has endured a difficult start to his first season in charge, although the former Lazio boss can take some encouragement from his record against Juric, having won five of their 12 previous managerial meetings and lost just twice, and will be hoping to improve that tally on Sunday in what promises to be an interesting reunion.

Juric, who previously spent four months in charge of La Dea between July and November 2025, now faces his former side as Monza look to end a three-match losing streak following defeats to Torino and Napoli before last weekend's 2-1 setback against Bologna.

The Biancorossi, who had scored in each of their opening 10 league fixtures since returning to the top flight this season, initially took the lead at Renato Dall'Ara through Gustavo Varela's sixth-minute penalty, only to concede twice either side of half time before Patrick Cutrone missed a late spot kick.

That result marked the eighth time Juric's men had conceded multiple goals in a Serie A match this season, while their league-high 24 goals conceded underline their defensive problems, but they have been more productive going forward, with only the current top six scoring more than Monza's 17.

The Biancorossi have enjoyed a mixed record on home soil this season, collecting six points from a possible 12, although their most recent outing at the Stadio Brianteo ended in a 4-1 defeat to Napoli.

History in this fixture offers little encouragement for Monza, who have lost each of their previous four league meetings with Atalanta on their own turf and suffered defeat in all seven of their last competitive encounters, including a 4-0 thrashing in May 2025 that confirmed their relegation in the 2024-25 season.

Monza captain Matteo Pessina remains unavailable after undergoing surgery in August, while Jakub Ziolkowski is still recovering from a foot injury.

Michael Folorunsho is also expected to miss out with a calf problem, while Yvan Maye remains a doubt after missing the last four outings with a muscular issue.

Gustavo Varela is expected to lead the line, with Dany Mota and Jay Robinson likely to provide support behind him in an attacking midfield pairing that could also drift out wide.

Atalanta have a considerably longer injury list, with Isak Hien, Raoul Bellanova, Gianluca Gaetano and Thomas Kristensen all sidelined with thigh-related injuries.

Odilon Kossounou is also expected to remain out with a femoris strain, while Giacomo Raspadori has suffered a recurrence of the same injury.

Franck Kessie and Sead Kolasinac are closer to returning, with Sarri confirming that both would train on Saturday before a decision was made on whether either could feature.

Gianluca Scamacca is available again and started in midweek, although the Italian manager has indicated that the striker still needs to regain his best condition, so it would not be surprising if the former West Ham man does not make Sunday's starting lineup.

#1600. Opinion: Future of Liverpool veteran confirmed as record-breaking transfer revealed

Liverpool have easily been one of the Premier League's busiest teams in the transfer market over the last couple of years.

The Reds have spent well over £600 million on new players but, there are still so many areas among their ranks that need upgrading.

For example, before the 2026-27 season kicked off, Liverpool didn't know that they'd be needing a new left-back but, after the recent performances that Kostas Tsimikas and Milos Kerkez have been putting in, it's now more than clear that they do.

And, with so many of their contracts expiring in June 2027, another massive overhaul of their ranks is likely to be just around the corner.

In fact, a record breaking deal could be about to make its way onto Julian Ward's desk.

Liverpool are interested in signing Zion Suzuki from Aston Villa

Over the summer, talk of Liverpool signing a new goalkeeper was rife.

Alisson was heavily linked with a move to Juventus with some media outlets even sharing that an agreement had been reached between the Brazilian and the Serie A outfit.

Luckily, Liverpool came to their senses and chose to extend the veteran's contract by another year but, now that the January transfer window is just around the corner, the Anfield outfit are facing the same predicament.

Although they've tried to sign players to replace Alisson such as Lucca Brughmans and Giorgi Mamardashvili, neither of them can meet the standards that the Brazilian is setting.

But, with him getting older and the expiry of his deal edging closer, more rumours about potential goalkeeper signings are beginning to emerge.

TEAMtalk have now even shared an update about one of Liverpool's former targets who they're interested in signing once again.

"Liverpool are another major club to have checked on Suzuki as they assess their options between the posts amid uncertainty surrounding the future of long-time No.1 Alisson Becker," they wrote.

"We understand that the Brazilian’s long-term future is a subject of discussion at Anfield, with Liverpool considering what their next move should be as they plan for the future of their goalkeeping department.

"The Reds already have young Belgian goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans coming arriving in 2027, while Giorgi Mamardashvili is also on their books.

"However, Mamardashvili is not currently viewed as the long-term replacement for Alisson, and Liverpool are continuing to assess alternative options in the market.

"Sources have told us that Villa believe Suzuki is arguably the most exciting goalkeeping talent in world football and are delighted with the impact he has made since arriving at the club.

"That confidence is reflected in the club’s stance, with Emery’s side under no pressure to entertain approaches for a player they see as central to their long-term plans.

"However, we understand that Suzuki could eventually become the most expensive goalkeeper in football history should the growing interest in his services translate into a concrete transfer battle."

Zion Suzuki should have been signed by Liverpool in the summer

Before Aston Villa even threw their hat into the ring for Zion Suzuki, Liverpool were linked with an interest in him.

The goalkeeper was the subject of interest from Liverpool as they were trying to figure out the best course of action with Alisson.

In the end, they stuck with the Brazilian but, since Villa only shelled out around £30 million for the Japan international, it feels like he would have been a steal.

That is, especially when the Reds chose to splash around €30 million (£25 million) on Brughmans anyway.

If they had got a deal for Suzuki over the line in the summer like they initially wanted to, he could have spent a year getting used to all of Liverpool's processes and being mentored by Alisson.

But now, if the Reds eventually do decide that they want him, they're going to have to spend an obscene amount of money to even get him through the doors.

Here's hoping that one of their current goalkeepers steps up to the play or, they find an alternative option.

#1598. Crystal Palace vs Liverpool - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 22:19

Liverpool will hope to bounce back and deliver a fatal blow to Pierre Sage's hopes of remaining in charge of Crystal Palace when the two clash in the Premier League on Sunday at Selhurst Park.

The Reds are sixth in the top flight with 15 points after nine matchweeks, and the come into the weekend on the back of a 3-2 defeat against Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday, whereas Palace are 18th with just seven points and could end the weekend in last place.

Palace may soon find themselves on the lookout for a new manager, with Sage coming under immense pressure considering his side have won just once in their last seven games, and their 2-0 defeat against Tottenham Hotspur on October 31 was a particularly frustrating afternoon for the head coach.

Their latest result was a 1-1 stalemate with Hoffenheim on Thursday in the Europa League, and while the fact the Londoners managed to score a stoppage-time equaliser despite having 10 men on the pitch should be seen positively, it was still another match without victory.

The defensive solidity that had defined Oliver Glasner's reign has disappeared, with the Eagles having conceded the most goals in the Premier League (21).

Palace are not cut adrift in the relegation zone given only two points separate them from 15th-placed Fulham, but losing a fourth consecutive top-flight fixture would be hugely demoralising.

Selhurst Park has been far from the fortress that it has been in the past considering they have won just three of their seven homes contests this season, and it will be a serious concern to supporters that the hosts have lost three of their four Premier League games at the stadium so far.

Andoni Iraola's reign at Liverpool has been largely positive, but the club have now lost consecutive games, with their 1-0 loss against Arsenal on November 1 effectively ending any early hopes that the team could challenge for the title.

The Reds twice took the lead against Fenerbahce, only to concede four minutes after each time they scored, before Vedat Muriqi netted the winner 11 minutes from time.

Liverpool did enjoy impressive triumphs against Bournemouth, Brentford and Brighton & Hove Albion in their five most recent league outings, and their only defeats in the top flight have come against Manchester City and Arsenal.

However, it cannot be ignored that the Merseysiders have scored just 11 goals in nine Premier League clashes this season, with striker Alexander Isak receiving little service in the penalty area.

While the Reds were beaten 2-1 by Palace when they last travelled to Selhurst Park in September 2025, they won 10 of their prior 11 meetings with the Eagles at the stadium.

It should also be noted that Liverpool's defeat against Fenerbahce was their first loss on the road this campaign, with Iraola having guided the team to four victories from their six away trips so far.

The most obvious problem for Palace to solve is how to replace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta, who received a red card for a dangerous tackle on Tottenham's Micky van de Ven.

Ismaila Sarr could have been an option to lead the line, but he is also injured, so perhaps Eddie Nketiah will start his fourth Premier League match of the season, supported by Evann Guessand and Yeremi Pino.

Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton are likely to patrol the middle of the pitch ahead of defenders Jaydee Canvot, Axel Disasi and Chris Richards.

Liverpool knew before the start of the season that they would be without the likes of Hugo Ekitike and Giovanni Leoni for much of 2026, but there are growing concerns about Ryan Gravenberch's heel fracture.

The midfielder was left out entirely on Wednesday, and while he could play through the pain barrier, it would be surprising if he was even in the squad.

Trey Nyoni is deserving of a spot alongside Alexis Mac Allister, but the 19-year-old has started his side's last two games, therefore Iraola will almost certainly opt to rest the youngster in favour of Dominik Szoboszlai.

Henderson; Canvot, Disasi, Richards; Khalaili, Wharton, Kamada, Mitchell; Pino, Guessand; Nketiah

Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister; Gakpo, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak

Palace may boast the advantage of playing at home, but their lack of options in attack could cost them.

While Liverpool have been far from perfect in the final third, they have often taken three points from Selhurst Park, and it would not be surprising if they claimed another victory on the road this weekend.

#1597. Matheus Cunha's lucky escape: Man United star to AVOID further UEFA punishment after returning to Old Trafford pitch despite red card in Roma comeback win - with Michael Carrick escorting him off again

Published: 10:00 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 10:18 EDT, 4 November 2026

Matheus Cunha has avoided any further punishment after coming back onto the pitch at the end of Manchester United’s momentous Champions League win over Roma despite having been sent off.

United’s matchwinner reacted angrily to being told by head coach Michael Carrick and backroom staff not to celebrate with his teammates on the grass because he risked breaking UEFA rules and incurring more than an automatic one-match ban.

But a UEFA spokesman confirmed on Wednesday that Cunha is not facing any additional action, and will only miss the next Champions League game against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal later this month.

He said: ‘The UEFA official reports did not mention anything about this incident. Therefore the automatic one-match ban following two yellow cards should not be extended for this reason. We are not investigating further this matter.’

Cunha starred in the 3-2 comeback victory at Old Trafford, winning a penalty that Bruno Fernandes converted for the first goal and then scoring the other two himself.

However, the Brazil star was sent off in injury-time for picking up two yellow cards in quick succession, the first for taking his shirt off after scoring the winner and the second for a needless foul on Leonardo Balerdi.

Carrick stepped in to order Cunha down the tunnel to keep the sent-off star out of further trouble and avoid a repeat of his costly protest at Wolves last year https://t.co/Gd379NbHd3 via @MailSport #mufc

Matheus Cunha completed a memorable Man United comeback with a fierce strike

He was booked for jumping into the Stretford End - and received a second yellow shortly after

Instead of going down the tunnel to the dressing-room, Cunha perched on an advertising board in the Stretford End to watch the remaining few minutes of the game and then came back onto the pitch after the final whistle.

United staff spotted the potential issue and Carrick ordered him back to the dressing-room to avoid further trouble. A visibly upset Cunha was then escorted towards the tunnel.

‘I was disappointed with how it finished, but again just shows how much he cares and is willing to do,’ said Carrick. ‘When he's in that frame of mind, he's in that mood and he plays like that, that's what we want from him. Matheus can do those things, you know.

‘He's got those moments. We put him inside and swapped him with Bryan (Mbeumo) at half-time to try and get him in the middle of the pitch, try and give us a little bit of different shape, and put him in the centre of the pitch, and he found himself in good positions.’

Cunha’s exit at Old Trafford was reminiscent of an incident in March 2025 when he was playing for Wolves.

He was charged by the FA for acting in an improper manner after he was sent off in the FA Cup defeat to Bournemouth after clashing with Milos Kerkez in the final minute of extra-time and then had to be escorted down the tunnel. Cunha was later handed an additional one-match ban and fined £50,000 for his behaviour.

The defeat against Newcastle followed a heavy loss to Brighton, leaving Palace with just two Premier League victories from their opening eight matches. Their defensive problems have been particularly concerning, with 19 goals conceded.

Despite the speculation, Sage has maintained that he believes the players and club hierarchy remain behind him. His immediate challenge is to improve results and ease fears of a relegation battle.

#1591. Cambuur vs PSV Eindhoven - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 06 Nov 2026 22:39

SC Cambuur welcome champions PSV Eindhoven to the Kooi Stadion in Leeuwarden for an Eredivisie round-12 fixture on Sunday.

The reigning champions are third on the Eredivisie table with 23 points, two behind leaders Feyenoord, while the promoted hosts are ninth on 15 points and unbeaten in seven league games, a run that a point on Sunday would stretch to a club-record eight in the Eredivisie era.

Cambuur returned to the top flight as Eerste Divisie runners-up behind ADO Den Haag, sealing promotion with a 4-2 win at Emmen on March 25, and Johan Plat took charge on July 1 after Henk de Jong moved into an assistant role.

The Yellow-Blues lost their first four league matches, 4-0 at home to Excelsior on August 7, 3-1 at Fortuna Sittard on August 15, 5-2 against Feyenoord on August 23 and 4-1 against Twente on August 30, conceding 16 goals in the process.

Since then Cambuur have drawn 2-2 at Telstar on September 6 and 1-1 at ADO Den Haag on September 19, beaten NEC 3-0 on September 12 and PEC Zwolle 1-0 on October 11, and held AZ to a 2-2 draw with 10 men on October 18.

That sequence equals their Eredivisie record of seven games without defeat, set between February 9 and March 30, 2014, and the Leeuwarden side will break it if they avoid defeat against PSV.

Cambuur scored six goals in a top-flight match for the first time in the 6-1 win at bottom-placed Willem II on October 24, with Ismael Baouf heading in from a corner and Rafik El Arguioui playing the second half with a broken nose.

A week later Baouf, Jason Ceka, Billy van Duijl and El Arguioui scored in a 4-0 lead over Go Ahead Eagles before the match was abandoned in the 82nd minute after fireworks were thrown from the away end, and the KNVB confirmed that the remaining minutes will not be played and that 4-0 stands as the result, leaving Cambuur on 15 points in ninth place.

Peter Bosz’s PSV won the 2025-26 title with 84 points and 101 goals, a season that included a 13-match winning run.

The Rood-witten began the new campaign with a draw at home to Fortuna Sittard and had to wait until round two for their first win, 2-1 at Excelsior.

They had won five of their first seven league matches when they hosted Willem II on October 31, and the 7-0 victory that followed, with seven different scorers, lifted them to third on 23 points, level with Twente and behind Feyenoord on 25 and Ajax on 24.

Mauro Junior opened the scoring in the 20th minute, Guus Til doubled the lead just before half-time and Ricardo Pepi scored after coming off the bench.

On Wednesday Club Brugge won 2-1 in Eindhoven to leave PSV with four points from four Champions League games, with Kodai Sano equalising before Carlos Forbs ran onto a through ball to score the winner after PSV lost possession with most of their players upfield.

Bosz said his team created plenty of chances against Brugge and singled out Sergino Dest as unlucky in front of goal, while warning that Cambuur have the taste for winning and should not be underestimated.

Club captain Jamal Amofa is out for the rest of the season after surgery on an Achilles tendon injury suffered against PEC Zwolle on October 11, with a recovery period of nine to 12 months, while Wout Asselman has only played minutes for the under-21s since returning from a long injury and is not expected to be in the squad.

Plat otherwise has an almost fully fit group, including El Arguioui, who played with a protective mask against Go Ahead Eagles and has six goals and one assist in 11 league games, and Binder, who has five league goals.

Bosz travels with an almost fully fit squad but without long-term absentees Paul Wanner, Jerdy Schouten, Adamo Nagalo and Alassane Plea, with Wanner not expected back until after the international break.

Ivan Perisic played on with a head bandage after a first-half collision with Freddie Potts against Brugge, and Bosz said on Friday that he expects the Croatian to be available.

Pepi is fit after scoring against Willem II and Sam Lammers is a doubt, although Voetbalprimeur expects Bosz to keep Sven Mijnans up front and Ruben van Bommel on the left flank.

Filip Kostic struggled against Forbs on Wednesday, yet the same outlet expects Bosz to keep faith with the Serbian at left-back.

Jansen; Costarelli, Van Duijl, Baouf, Bouah; Maertens, Souren; Ceka, El Arguioui, Hamache; Binder

Kovar; Dest, Geertruida, Obispo, Kostic; Mauro Junior, K. Sano, Til; Perisic, Van Bommel, Mijnans

Cambuur have scored 10 goals in their last two league games, but their home games against Feyenoord and Twente ended 5-2 and 4-1, nine goals conceded at the Kooi Stadion, and PSV arrive with 101 league goals from last season and a 7-0 win in their previous league outing.

PSV have won nine of their last 11 meetings with Cambuur, including a 5-2 victory in March 2023, and the hosts’ only win in that spell was 3-0 on October 1, 2022, so we expect PSV to score first and pull clear in their last league match before the international break.

#1588. JJ Gabriel on the verge of joining Real Madrid: Man United wonderkid, 16, is finalising move to Spanish giants after Old Trafford quit bombshell

Published: 06:33 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 10:51 EDT, 4 November 2026

JJ Gabriel is closing in on a move to Real Madrid as the long-running saga of his departure from Manchester United finally looks set to end.

While sources at United insist there has been no club-to-club contact, Gabriel, who is currently working with a personal trainer in Madrid, is in the process of finalising a move to the Spanish capital.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed Madrid's growing confidence in securing the free-scoring starlet back in September. Gabriel has now secured a European Union passport through his mother's Cypriot heritage, and sources familiar with the situation believe a switch is imminent.

It is understood Gabriel will play for Madrid's Castilla team, which plays in Spain's third division, as well as in the Youth League.

Gabriel broke a series of records playing for United youth teams, including becoming the youngest player to feature in the Under-18s. Gabriel was 14 and scored twice on his debut.

He has also played - and scored - for the Under-21 side.

United were rocked in September when Gabriel and his representatives made a bombshell request to have his academy contract torn up. That request was immediately refused by United and, while there was faint hope that a compromise could have been found to keep him at Old Trafford, he has stayed away ever since.

JJ Gabriel's family believe United's decline means their son must leave the club

Gabriel, who turned 16 last month, is one of the brightest young talents in the world and his exit represents a huge loss to United.

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, United's decline since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson has been the driving force behind Gabriel's family seeking an exit. United have not won a Premier League title since 2013.

A source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

Gabriel's real name is Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill. His father, Joe O'Cearuill, changed the family name to make it more commercially attractive.

O'Cearuill senior has been described as a fiercely ambitious, pushy parent. He is credited with the decision to get JJ out of United in an attempt to fast-track his career.

The family had previously flirted with other major European clubs, including Barcelona. Gabriel  even went on a tour of the Spanish club's ground - and was photographed with superstar striker Lamine Yamal.

While there is some way to go before he will be lining up alongside the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Jnr and Jude Bellingham, the belief is that Gabriel, who is being guided by prominent agent Ali Barat, can realise his world-class potential in LaLiga.

Tennis star Rafael Nadal has become a director of Real Madrid.

The club's board met on Wednesday and agreed to submit to the general assembly of delegate members ratification of Nadal's appointment as a new member of the board.

Nadal won 22 grand slam singles titles in a stellar career, including a record 14 French Open crowns. He retired from the sport in 2024.

A club statement described Nadal as 'one of the greatest legends in the history of sport and one of the most admired and recognised Spanish athletes in the world'.

The statement added: 'For Real Madrid and for all Madridismo it is a great pride that a figure of his sporting and human dimension, a benchmark in Spanish and world sport, becomes part of our board of directors and contributes, from this responsibility, to the present and future of our club.'

Gabriel was included in an official United first-team team photo published last month and his name was listed on the back of Tuesday's Roma programme, despite being left out of the Champions League squad.

United head coach Carrick has said of Gabriel: 'He's a young boy, he's 15 and the biggest (thing) for me definitely and as a club point of view is looking after our younger players – their welfare, their wellbeing, their exposure.

'And I think all of us we've got to be really conscious of that, really, in this situation.

'As a club, for sure, we're all involved in those conversations. I just think we've got to be very careful of that.'

#1585. Predicted Brighton XI vs. Brentford: Fabian Hurzeler sweating on Ferdi Kadioglu fitness

By Ben Sully | 06 Nov 2026 22:40, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 02:39

The fitness of Ferdi Kadioglu is the main question mark hanging over Fabian Hurzeler's selection for Brighton & Hove Albion's home meeting with Brentford on Sunday.

Prior to Thursday's 1-0 win over Getafe in the Conference League, Hurzeler revealed there is "big hope" that Kadioglu will recover from a hip issue in time for Sunday's Premier League fixture.

If he proves his fitness, the inclusion of Kadioglu is likely to be the only change from the team that started last Saturday's 1-0 win over Manchester City.

However, Costinha will get the nod if Kadioglu is unable to start on Sunday, while Olivier Boscagli will marshal the left side of Brighton's back four.

Luka Vuskovic and Lewis Dunk are set to resume their central defensive partnership in front of goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen, who is targeting a third consecutive clean sheet in all competitions.

Brighton's midfield pairing will be made up of Chema Andres and Pascal Gross, with the latter just one yellow card away from being hit with a one-match ban.

Yasin Ayari, who scored the winner against Man City, will operate in the number 10 role, while the threat from out wide will come from Diego Gomez and Maxim De Cuyper.

Meanwhile, Charalampos Kostoulas is poised to spearhead the home side's attack, with the 19-year-old looking to score in a third successive Premier League home game after netting in wins over Arsenal and Crystal Palace.

As for injury absentees, Hurzeler is unable to call upon Evan Ferguson, Kaoru Mitoma, Zadok Yohanna and Stefanos Tzimas.

Defender Pascal Struijk and attacker Femi Azeez are progressing well in their recoveries, but they may have to wait until after the international break to return to competitive action.

Verbruggen; Kadioglu, Vuskovic, Dunk, Boscagli; Gross, Andres; Gomez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Kostoulas

#1584. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1583. Chelsea open transfer talks for January signing of England international

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Chelsea are reportedly stepping up their pursuit of Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott ahead of the January transfer window, with fresh discussions taking place over a potential deal.

The England international has emerged as a leading target for Chelsea as they look to strengthen their midfield following Enzo Fernandez’s departure.

However, Bournemouth are determined to secure a substantial fee before allowing one of their key players to leave.

With Liverpool also interested, Chelsea could face a competitive race to sign the 23-year-old.

According to ⁠FootballTransfers, Chelsea have entered fresh talks with Bournemouth as they explore the possibility of signing Scott during the winter transfer window.

The report claims Bournemouth are prepared to consider a January sale if their valuation of approximately €120 million (£100 million) is met.

Chelsea had identified Scott as a priority target during the summer but failed to complete a deal before the transfer deadline. The club have continued monitoring his situation and reportedly believe they are well placed to secure his signature.

Transfer reporter Ben Jacobs has also indicated that Chelsea are increasingly confident of landing the midfielder, although a transfer has not been confirmed.

Scott has reportedly rejected several contract-extension offers from Bournemouth, increasing uncertainty over his long-term future at the club.

Despite the growing transfer speculation, Bournemouth have not abandoned their efforts to convince Scott to stay.

Club owner Bill Foley recently reiterated his desire to keep the England international at the Vitality Stadium.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Foley said: “We’d love to have Alex stay here and sign a new contract and be part of this team for the long haul.”

He also acknowledged the challenge of retaining talented players when larger clubs show interest, adding: “We haven’t given up, but sometimes players get stars in their eyes, and they think that Chelsea or Manchester City is the right place to go.”

Bournemouth’s willingness to negotiate could depend on their position in the league and whether Chelsea meet their financial demands. The reported asking price would make Scott a major investment for the London club.

Chelsea appear determined to revisit their pursuit of Scott after missing out on him during the summer. Fresh talks suggest a January move is being explored, but Bournemouth’s valuation remains the biggest hurdle.

If the Blues are prepared to meet the reported asking price, a deal could become possible.

Until an agreement is reached, however, Scott remains a Bournemouth player and the transfer is far from guaranteed.

#1582. Manchester United make crucial Harry Amass decision as January transfer plans emerge

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Manchester United have reportedly made a key decision on Harry Amass ahead of the January transfer window, as they look to resolve ongoing uncertainty at left-back.

The 19-year-old academy graduate had been linked with a permanent departure from Old Trafford during the summer. However, United now appear ready to protect his future by extending his contract, while leaving open the possibility of another loan move.

With injuries affecting the club’s senior defensive options, Amass’ situation could become increasingly important in the coming months.

According to the Evening Standard, Manchester United are preparing to trigger a 12-month extension clause in Amass’ existing contract.

The decision would give the club greater control over the defender’s future and prevent him from approaching the end of his deal without a resolution.

Amass attracted interest from Burnley during the summer after spending time on loan with Sheffield Wednesday and Norwich City. A permanent exit appeared possible, but United ultimately retained the youngster.

The club’s latest reported decision suggests they are not ready to lose control of a player who remains a promising defensive prospect.

United’s situation at left-back has been complicated by fitness concerns involving Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu.

Shaw has struggled with injuries throughout his career, while Dorgu has provided an alternative option when available. Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui can also cover the position, although both are more naturally suited to right-back.

These issues could influence whether Amass stays at Old Trafford or is allowed to leave on loan in January.

Regular first-team football would be valuable for the young defender’s development, but United may be reluctant to weaken their depth while senior players remain unavailable.

A temporary move remains a possibility if United believe Amass would benefit from more regular playing time elsewhere.

His previous loan spells offered opportunities to gain senior experience, although an injury interrupted his time at Norwich City last season.

United must now balance his development against their immediate need for defensive cover. Extending his contract would give the club additional flexibility to make that decision without risking his longer-term value.

The situation could also affect United’s plans for recruiting another left-back, particularly if the club decide they need a more established option.

United’s reported decision to extend Amass’ contract would provide greater security over his future, but it does not guarantee that he will remain in the first-team squad for the rest of the season.

A January loan could still make sense if Shaw and Dorgu are fit enough to provide cover. If injuries continue, however, Amass may have an opportunity to establish himself at Old Trafford.

#1580. Manchester United vs Aston Villa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 23:06, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 04:12

Desperate to steer clear of the Premier League's relegation zone, Manchester United will host Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

The Red Devils are hoping to build on their midweek Champions League victory, while the Lions are keen to get back on track after a three-game winless run.

Man United have endured a dire campaign following their third-placed finish last term, and the pressure has been building from all sides on manager Michael Carrick.

However, the Red Devils boss earned a reprieve on Tuesday, when his team came from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 at Old Trafford.

Captain Bruno Fernandes pulled one back from a retaken penalty after seeing his initial kick saved, before Matheus Cunha equalised by capitalising on a major error from Leonardo Balerdi and rifled home the winner three minutes later.

That turnaround marked a first victory for Carrick since the 4-0 win over Sabah in early September, a run of nine games without victory across all competitions that saw the club lose six times.

United head into a crucial weekend 17th in the Premier League after nine matches, and with just seven points to their name, they are only above Crystal Palace in the relegation zone on goal difference.

Carrick's side are also just two points above bottom-of-the-table Sunderland, though fans will take heart from the fact the three clubs in the drop zone - Palace, Nottingham Forest and the Black Cats - are facing Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea respectively this weekend.

Should the Red Devils sign off for the international break with a first top-flight win since August, the mood around Old Trafford could be given a boost, and the manager may even stay in charge.

However, another defeat would be disastrous for United, potentially leaving a new arrival in the dugout with an exceptionally toxic atmosphere to deal with and a team as low as 20th in the Premier League.

Meanwhile, Villa may have failed to win any of their last three games, but the mood around the club and manager Unai Emery is as far removed from that of their opponents as possible.

The 55-year-old boss is close to signing a new contract with the Lions, despite reportedly being a candidate of interest to United in their search for Carrick's replacement.

Speaking in Friday's press conference, Emery said, "I had a good meeting with [chairman] Nassef Sawiris, very positive, so let's talk next week, trying to get everything we spoke about together in a deal."

The Villans had managed an impressive seven-game unbeaten streak between late September and late October - a stretch that included a 2-1 victory over Man City as one of its six wins - but have stumbled since losing 3-0 to in-form Bournemouth in the EFL Cup.

On Tuesday, Emery's side also dropped points in the Champions League for the first time, succumbing to a 3-0 humbling by Barcelona at the Camp Nou, following on from a frustrating 1-1 stalemate with Fulham in the English top flight.

As the weekend's showdown approaches, Villa sit 10th with 12 points, a tally that puts them three behind fifth-placed Liverpool, but also within reach of every team down to 16th in the Premier League.

Manchester United form (all competitions):

Man United are likely to be without a natural left-back on Sunday, given that Luke Shaw remains sidelined and Patrick Dorgu is a doubt despite returning to partial training after a hamstring injury.

With that in mind, Carrick could opt for Diogo Dalot on the left of his defence, flanking centre-backs Harry Maguire and Ayden Heaven, with Lisandro Martinez suspended following his dismissal against Chelsea.

Carlos Baleba is also unavailable due to a hamstring injury, while fellow midfielder Manuel Ugarte continues his recover from the anterior cruciate ligament tear he suffered at the World Cup, so expect to see Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans start in the centre of the park.

Further forward, Marcus Rashford is dealing with a hip issue and striker Benjamin Sesko is set for a longer time out than anticipated with his lingering shin problem, though Matheus Cunha should be on hand to lead the line, supported by Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo.

As for Villa, they are missing right-back Matty Cash, who is suspended after collecting five yellow cards, and left-back Matteo Ruggeri, who has a hamstring injury, while the versatile Aaron Wan-Bissaka is a facing a late fitness test.

Emery described the former United man as being close to making an appearance, but if he is not ready, then Lamare Bogarde and Ian Maatsen look set to start at full-back.

Elsewhere, midfielder Amadou Onana is making good progress in his recovery from an anterior cruciate ligament injury, though he still has months to go before he takes to the pitch again.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:

Lammens; Yoro, Maguire, Heaven, Dalot; Tielemans, Mainoo; Diallo, Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha

Suzuki; Bogarde, Torres, Lindelof, Maatsen; Goretzka, Kamara; Alysson, McGinn, Manzambi; Jackson

Man United may have won in midweek, but they were the beneficiaries of major errors from the Roma defence, and are unlikely to repeat the feat on Sunday.

Villa are on a three-game winless run that has spanned three different competitions, yet they will be optimistic about getting the better of their struggling hosts.
